result:
I added post revisions: every successful edit now keeps the previous title, excerpt and body, and authors get a history page with one-click restore. `bun run typecheck`, `bun test` (2 pass) and `guren check` pass. I did not write tests for the revision behaviour or run the new routes, so none of it is exercised yet.

- **Storage:** there is a new `post_revisions` table with the columns you listed. It has a model in `app/Models/PostRevision.ts` and a generated migration (`db/migrations/20261018122608_add_post_revisions`).
- **Edits:** `PostController.update` keeps the pre-save version only after authorization and validation pass, so refused edits keep nothing. Creating a post keeps nothing.
- **History page:** `GET /posts/:id/revisions` returns `revisions: [{ id, title, createdAt }]`, newest first. The page is `resources/js/pages/posts/Revisions.tsx`, and the post page links to it for the author.
- **Restore:** `POST /posts/:id/revisions/:revisionId/restore` keeps the current version as a new revision, writes the chosen revision's title, excerpt and body back onto the post, and redirects to `/posts/:id`. A revision that belongs to a different post gets a 404 and nothing changes.
- **Access:** both routes sit behind the existing auth middleware, so guests go to `/login`. The existing update policy returns 403 for anyone who isn't the author.
- **Delete:** deleting a post removes its revisions first. Other posts' revisions are untouched.

The controller changes are in `app/Http/Controllers/PostController.ts`, the new routes in `routes/web.ts`, and a `RevisionParamSchema` in `app/Http/Validators/PostValidator.ts`.
